description:
runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:749 copies the suffix bytes to a Vec so alloc_bitstring (&mut self) can be called, which copies them again into the heap. The comment says the copy is for the borrow; the slice comes from from_raw_parts on an off-heap immovable buffer, so its lifetime is not tied to self. runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1516 does the same for an aligned binary field (the unaligned BitWriter arm really builds new bytes and keeps its Vec).
Before building: confirm alloc_bitstring / alloc_kind (imp.rs:690) cannot collect or move the source between reading the slice and copying it. If it can, stop and report.
Shape: pass the slice straight through; delete the comment that explained the copy.
Heat: every <<c, rest::binary>> step on a small binary and every aligned binary field read, at program run time.

Method: .agent/strategies/ownership-shape.md. Change the signature and let cargo check enumerate dependents; resolve interleavings by compute-then-commit or a split borrow; stop and report if an Rc is the only move.
Signal: pure refactor. Full gate green; no golden, census or pin moves. Report the clone/to_vec count of each touched file before and after.
Sites were read at develop 8bf8775ae and not compiled; confirm each with cargo check before relying on it.
title: A bitstring read copies its bytes once
